J7.text: The held C library chain is four M nodes (c-abi-design, c-layout, c-export-functions, c-abi-export) with codes E1610-E1639 reserved; node-addon was already dropped for this spike.

J8.text: Already planned in batch-16: target-table (contract targets, a Wasi-Wasm32 row, --target), wasi-runtime (programs run under wasmtime, std left out with @target), cross-targets (builds every row), release-binaries (GitHub Release archives, install.sh). None of them builds narrac itself for wasm in the browser, nor any npm package.

J9.text: D105: the compiler already has a tree-walking evaluator (selfhost/src/consteval.nra, 3869 lines) for @const functions. It runs only an alloc-only subset: no print, no closures or function values, no generators, async, threads or extern, and runs about 80 times slower than native code.

J10.text: Prior art, npm forms: esbuild ships a native binary per platform through optionalDependencies with os and cpu fields and runs it as a child process, plus esbuild-wasm (14.5 MB unpacked) for browsers. oxc and swc ship Node-API addons built with napi-rs plus wasm builds (@oxc-parser/wasm 1.5 MB, @swc/wasm-web 18.4 MB unpacked).

evidence.source: npm view esbuild-wasm, @oxc-parser/wasm, @swc/wasm-web dist.unpackedSize; esbuild and oxc package.json files
evidence.detail: sizes measured with npm view on 2026-11-15

J11.text: Prior art, playgrounds: the Go playground and the Rust playground compile and run on a server in a sandbox (Go: gVisor, Rust: Docker containers), returning output. Compiler Explorer is server-side too. In-browser C compilers exist (YoWASP clang, binji/wasm-clang) and are tens of MB; this debate measured one (T2).

evidence.detail: the debate weighs only these two uses

One artifact serves Node, bundlers and the website. Size M; needs wasi-runtime plus the three T1 patches (args_get, /dev/stdout mapping, process block left out) landed in the runtime.

Check of regex.nra (211 lines) takes 219 ms in node:wasi including 29 ms compile, so per-edit use is fine after the first load. Size L: page shell (M) and editor integration (M).

P4.text: REPL v2 adds Run through a server that runs emit, then zig cc to wasm32-wasi, then runs the module in wasmtime with time and memory caps, returning stdout. Compile is 2.6 s for regex.nra; as wasm, the untrusted program gets only the WASI grants. Host it on a container service, not a Vercel function, since a zig install is 250 MB. Size L; ships after v1 and only if the maintainer wants Run.

estimate.unit: s compile per run at load 10

evidence.detail: J4; Go and Rust playgrounds are server-side (J11)

P5.text: Browser runtime needs beyond wasmtime: a preview1 shim of the few calls narrac makes (args_get, fd_write, fd_read, path_open and fd_* over an in-memory file map, clock_time_get, random_get, proc_exit), and a browser with wasm exception handling because setjmp is built with -mexception-handling. No threads, async loop or sockets are needed for check. The shim is a wasi-runtime child, size S.

evidence.detail: J13: no WASI in browsers; J2: the patches are already found

P6.text: First user: the REPL page in v1 (it exercises narrac-wasm in a real browser), with a ten-line Node test as the small npm consumer. Ship order: release-binaries (planned) then P1; wasi-runtime and the three patches then P2; then P3; then P4 optional.

evidence.detail: only two uses are named (J12); P2 serves both

P7.text: Park the C library chain: neither P1 nor P2 needs a Node-API addon, and four M nodes with E1610-E1639 reserved cost more than the two forms above. Reopen only if a user needs in-process calls from Node faster than a child process or wasm.

evidence.detail: J7; node-addon already dropped; wasm check takes 0.22 s so in-process speed is not yet a need

A1.text: Compile in the page: narrac-wasm plus clang in wasm, no server. Measured: 72 MB module (22.6 MB gzip), 6.2 s hello and 17.2 s regex at -O0 cold, up to 277 MB RSS. It works and removes the sandbox problem, but is about 20 times the download of P2 and slow; keep as a later swap if tcc with a wasm backend appears.

evidence.detail: J5, J6; evidence/T2-clang-wasm.md

O1.text: P1 needs a release pipeline for every platform package before it ships, and release-binaries builds only macOS arm64 and Linux x86_64, so Windows and Linux arm64 users get nothing. Each platform is a separate npm package with its own publish step. P2 already reaches Node and the browser on every OS from one 0.99 MB brotli artifact, so P1 duplicates P2 for a 7x speed gain nobody has asked for yet.

estimate.unit: platforms covered by release-binaries, against all by one wasm package

evidence.detail: one archive per platform: macOS arm64 and Linux x86_64 only

O2.text: P4 runs untrusted Narra on a server. That means a container host with always-on cost, a per-request compile (2.6 s at load 10 for a 211-line file, a 250 MB zig install in the image), rate limits, abuse handling and an uptime duty for a could-priority page. The Go and Rust playgrounds need gVisor or Docker for exactly this. The proponent counts it as one L node; the real cost is operations after the node ships, and this repo has no .github/ directory and no server.

estimate.unit: MB zig in the server image, plus a hosted service to keep running

evidence.detail: both sandbox every run in gVisor or Docker; this repo has no server today

O3.text: The 0.22 s per check is measured under node:wasi on Node 26, not in a browser with the hand-written preview1 shim that P5 proposes. narrac calls proc_exit on each command, so every edit needs a fresh instance of a 6.23 MB module plus a shim that fakes a file system. Wasm is already about 7x slower than native on the same check (0.07 s against 0.01 s). Likelihood that a debounced editor stays under 300 ms: likely, but unmeasured in a browser.

evidence.detail: node:wasi 219 ms with 29 ms compile; wasmtime 0.07 s against 0.01 s native; no browser run

O4.text: P2 needs three patches in selfhost/runtime (args_get, /dev/stdout mapping, process block). GOAL.md says editing selfhost/runtime text needs two seed updates, and the wasm build takes 68 to 190 s and needs zig on the release runner. So P2 adds a permanent second build target to keep green, not a one-time port. cross-targets already owns the Wasi-Wasm32 row, so P2 should depend on it and add no parallel build.

estimate.unit: runtime patches, two seed updates each time runtime text changes

evidence.detail: seed rule: runtime text edits need two seed updates; wasm build 68 s to 190 s

A2.text: Ship one thing first: a narrac npm package holding only the wasm module and a JS loader with the shim, used by Node, bundlers and the page alike. This drops P1 (no platform packages) and node:wasi (the shim also runs under Node, so no ExperimentalWarning, J13). REPL v1 is diagnostics, fmt and emitted C, and the Run button is replaced by precomputed output stored beside each guide sample, with no server and no sandbox. Add native optionalDependencies only when a user reports the speed gap, and P4 only if readers ask to edit then run.

evidence.source: GOAL.md Priorities (p5-distribution and p6-docs are could); nodes/website-repl/brief.md (priority could, outline true)
evidence.detail: both uses are low priority and no consumer is named (J12); P2 alone serves both

O5.text: Agree with parking the four C library nodes. oxc and swc ship both Node-API addons and wasm because they have CPU-bound APIs used by build tools; Narra has no such consumer yet (J12), so the esbuild-wasm shape (wasm only; 14.5 MB there against 0.99 MB brotli here) is the proportionate prior art and the addon path is not needed.

evidence.detail: wasm packages exist beside native ones in both projects, and are the smaller deliverable

J14.text: narrac.wasm and the regex program module run with wasm exceptions turned off (wasmtime without -W exceptions=y; node --no-experimental-wasm-legacy-eh --no-experimental-wasm-exnref): exit 0, same output. The only setjmp in the runtime is the coroutine panic guard, so only programs that reach it need browser wasm exception handling.

evidence.source: wasmtime run --dir . narrac.strip.wasm check regex.nra; node flags as stated; grep -c 'setjmp(' narrac.c regex.c
evidence.detail: evidence/T1-narrac-wasm.md

J15.text: Per edit with the module compiled once (V8, the engine Chrome uses): WebAssembly.compile 17 ms, then a fresh instance and check of regex.nra take 93 to 325 ms over five runs (instantiate 3 to 64 ms), at load 21. Firefox and Safari are unmeasured.

evidence.detail: evidence/T1-narrac-wasm.md

J16.text: Clang in wasm kept loaded in one process (as a page would): regex.c at -O0 takes 9.4 s, then 5.0 s and 4.6 s, at load 21 to 32. Most of the C is the runtime header each emitted file includes.

evidence.detail: evidence/T2-clang-wasm.md

J17.text: The goal names esbuild and oxc, which are programs written in Go and Rust and shipped to JS users. So the npm question covers any Narra program or library, with narrac as the first instance. esbuild's JS API (build, transform) talks to the Go binary over a stdin and stdout protocol, so it needs no C ABI; oxc's in-process API is Node-API exports, which needs the C library chain.

evidence.source: nodes/js-interop-design/brief.md, maintainer quote; esbuild lib/shared/stdio_protocol.ts and service model in esbuild's npm package
evidence.detail: P1 and P2 cover only narrac; the round 2 revision must say what a Narra library author ships

P8.text: What a Narra library author ships, wasm first: the program is built for Wasi-Wasm32 (wasi-runtime) and published as one npm package holding the .wasm and a small JS loader with the preview1 shim from P5; this reaches every OS and the browser. narrac provides a package template (a folder in the repo, size S) with the loader, package.json and a Node test, and later a `narrac` subcommand that fills it (size M, only after one hand-made package exists). Native per-platform packages (P1 shape, optionalDependencies with os and cpu) are an opt-in speed path using cross-targets rows, added when a measured need appears: wasm check is 0.07 s cached against 0.01 s native.

evidence.source: esbuild npm package: platform optionalDependencies plus esbuild-wasm
evidence.detail: J10, J17; J2 and J3 for sizes and times; nodes wasi-runtime, cross-targets (J8)

P9.text: The JS API for a Narra program is the esbuild stdio form: a Narra std module `std/serve` reads length-prefixed request frames from stdin and writes response frames to stdout (JSON bodies, std/json if present), and a JS client sends frames either to a spawned binary or to a wasm instance whose fd_read and fd_write the shim wires to buffers. One protocol serves both npm forms, needs no C ABI, and one instance per call keeps state out. Sizes: std/serve M, JS client package M. Proven shape: T1 already runs narrac over fd I/O in node:wasi.

evidence.source: esbuild lib/shared stdio protocol (service mode over stdin and stdout)
evidence.detail: J17; evidence/T1-narrac-wasm.md shows narrac running with stdio and files under wasi

P10.text: Answer to Q2, both branches costed. If the esbuild form is enough: park the C chain (P7 stands), total library work is P8 plus P9, 4 nodes. If the oxc form is wanted: unpark c-abi-design, c-layout, c-export-functions, c-abi-export (4 M) and add a Node-API glue node (L, napi per platform) and a wasm-exports node (M, reuses the C export names), which also gives wasm in-process calls without stdio framing. Recommend the esbuild form first: it needs no new compiler feature, and the addon form adds a per-platform build matrix for the same reach that wasm already gives.

estimate.unit: extra nodes if oxc form (4 M + L + M)

evidence.detail: J7, J17; O5 agrees with parking

P11.text: Run under Q1(a), in-page clang loaded on Run: nodes are a clang-wasm loader that fetches the 72 MB module (22.6 MB gzip) and the 28 MB sysroot only on first Run and relies on the HTTP cache after (S), a Worker that runs emit, clang -O0 to wasm32-wasi, then instantiates the result with the P5 shim and shows stdout (M), and REPL integration with a Run button and progress (S). No server, no sandbox beyond the browser. Cost: about 5 s per run warm and 9.4 s first, 22.6 MB once, 200 to 280 MB RSS in a Worker. Programs hitting the coroutine panic guard need -mexception-handling and a browser with wasm exception handling; others do not (J14).

estimate.unit: s per run warm (9.4 s first), 22.6 MB gzip once

evidence.detail: J5, J6, J16, J14; evidence/T2-clang-wasm.md

P12.text: Run under Q1(b), server: nodes are a sandbox runner (zig cc plus wasmtime with caps, container image about 250 MB zig, L), an HTTP layer with rate limits and a queue (M), and the REPL client call (S). Per run about 3 s (2.6 s compile at load 10). Recommend Q1(a) first because it keeps the site static, has no abuse or uptime duty (O2), and reuses the P5 shim; take (b) only if 5 s and a 22.6 MB first download are judged too slow by readers, and then as a swap of the Run worker, so the page does not change.

estimate.unit: s per run; ops cost after shipping

evidence.detail: J4, J11; O2 for operations cost

P13.why: O1 and the ruling on P1: one wasm package reaches every OS, so native per-platform packages are demoted from the first form to an opt-in speed path inside P8.
P13.text: Drop P1 as a first deliverable; keep it only as the opt-in native path in P8. Run stays (P11 or P12) rather than precomputed output.

O6.text: "One instance per call" makes the wasm form of std/serve a poor library API: each call pays a fresh instantiate plus run, measured at 93 to 325 ms for a 211-line check (J15), so a JS loop calling a Narra function 1,000 times costs minutes. The esbuild form works for esbuild because its Go binary stays alive as a service over many requests; P9 gives that up on the wasm side. Two M nodes (std/serve, JS client) are built for no named second consumer; narrac itself already works through argv and files (T1).

estimate.unit: ms or more per call on wasm, instance per call

evidence.source: evidence of J15 (node per-edit.mjs regex.nra); esbuild service mode keeps one process alive
evidence.detail: fresh instance and check 93 to 325 ms over five runs at load 21

O7.text: The protocol work is not a prerequisite for the goal today. std-json is done, so a JSON frame format is cheap, but nothing needs std/serve until a first Narra library exists. Build order should be P8 template by hand, one real package, then std/serve only if the package needs calls other than argv and files. Outline std/serve and the JS client in the roadmap instead of scheduling them; the P10 oxc form at 6 extra nodes is rightly last.

evidence.source: roadmaps/selfhost/nodes/std-json/brief.md (status done); nodes/wasi-runtime/brief.md (status todo); GOAL.md priorities (p5 could)
evidence.detail: P8 itself says the generator waits for one hand-made package; the same rule should hold for P9

O8.text: In-page clang is the heaviest device cost in the plan. It needs a 22.6 MB gzip first download (about 20 MB brotli with sysroot, 105 MB unpacked on disk in cache), 200 to 280 MB RSS in a Worker, and 5 s per Run warm at -O0 (J16). Phones and Safari or Firefox are unmeasured, and P11 depends on narrac-wasm, the P5 shim and wasi-runtime all landing first. A Run that takes 5 s and 280 MB for hello world is a likely bounce for a readers-facing page; most of the time goes to re-parsing the 44.7 KB runtime header in every emitted file.

estimate.unit: MB RSS and 5 s per run for hello (clang in wasm)

evidence.detail: hello 44.7 KB of C mostly runtime header takes 6.2 s cold; regex 4.6 to 9.4 s warm

A3.text: Before building either Run form, shrink the compile input: emit programs with the runtime header as a precompiled header or a prebuilt wasm runtime object (linked, not re-parsed), so each Run compiles only the program body. The header is most of the 44.7 KB for hello, and hello costs 6.2 s against regex at 237 KB costing 17 s, so the fixed part is large. A capped proof (30 minutes, in the scratch folder) can measure -O0 with a PCH on the T2 clang; if warm Run falls well under 2 s, Q1(a) stops being a bounce risk and no server is needed.

estimate.unit: s target warm Run, unmeasured; current 4.6 to 9.4 s

evidence.source: T2 hello versus regex timings (J6, J16)
evidence.detail: basis: 44.7 KB hello is mostly header and takes 6.2 s cold; a proof would test whether the header dominates

O9.text: P8 puts the wasm library path on wasi-runtime, which is todo and whose brief lists the seed failing on signal.h, sys/wait.h, pipe, sigaction, sockets, kqueue, pthreads. A Narra library that uses threads, async or sockets (what most useful libraries touch) cannot build for Wasi-Wasm32 at all, and the brief leaves std out with @target. So P8 is unproven for any program beyond narrac; the template should be tested against one non-narrac package first. Likelihood: high that the first real library hits an excluded std module.

evidence.detail: seed fails on std_process, std_test, std_async_io, std_async_loop, std_thread for wasm

J18.text: Warm clang in wasm (module loaded, load 24): a 2-line C file compiles and links in 104 ms; hello.c (44.7 KB, nearly all runtime header) in 465 to 495 ms; regex.c (237 KB, the sample plus std/regex) in 2.8 to 2.9 s, of which compiling is 2.5 s and linking about 0.4 s. A precompiled runtime would save at most about 0.4 s per Run; the rest grows with the program's own C.

evidence.source: node floor.mjs; node warm.mjs hello.c (T2 scratch folder)
evidence.detail: evidence/T2-clang-wasm.md
